findings.failure_mode: unreadable, missing, or permission-denied paths abort the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or a domain error type) and propagate with ? or explicit error handling

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked indexing into a Vec produced by split
findings.failure_mode: a line with zero or one comma-fragment panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to extract name and value parts, then handle the None case with a typed error instead of indexing

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy as-cast after an unwrap
findings.failure_mode: a parseable u32 value >65535 silently truncates to u16 via wrap-around; values that fit in u16 succeed but the as cast is hidden and unchecked
findings.fix: parse directly as u16 with .parse::<u16>(), or use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) with checked conversion and return a typed error on overflow; never use as for width reduction

findings.problem: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value for the value field
findings.failure_mode: a single malformed line (e.g., "alpha,abc") aborts the entire records collection instead of skipping or reporting the bad line
findings.fix: use .parse::<u16>() with map_err to return a typed ParseError, or use .ok_or_else() converting to a domain error type

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side effect inside the pure parsing pipeline
findings.failure_mode: logging inside the data-parsing function couples the core to I/O, makes testing harder, and produces output even when the caller does not want it
findings.fix: remove println! from the parsing closure; push logging to the imperative shell layer that calls load_quotes

findings.problem: load_quotes performs fs::read_to_string (imperative shell I/O) but returns Vec<Record> (a pure core type) with no error channel
findings.failure_mode: the function signature promises a pure Vec but actually performs IO and can panic; callers cannot handle errors at compile time
findings.fix: split into a shell function that reads and maps errors, and a pure core function that parses &str lines into Result<Record, ParseError>; return Result<Vec<Record>, Error> from the public API

findings.problem: Collects every split fragment into Vec<String> via .collect() when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation and string cloning for every line; also enables unchecked indexing pattern above
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get (name_part, value_part) without allocation, trim each part as &str, and parse directly

findings.problem: Record fields are pub and mutable by default (pub name: String, pub value: u16)
findings.failure_mode: callers can mutate parsed records after construction, violating the functional-core invariant that data is inert and valid by construction
findings.fix: make fields private (name: String, value: u16) and provide an impl block; or derive Debug/Serialize as needed behind an interface
